title: Every phenomenon this deposit touches, and the rule for the rest — 4 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Every phenomenon this deposit touches, and the rule for the rest. 4 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/phenomena.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 2 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 12 pairs; the theorems fall into 1 strand. Most binding: entries (4), statusOf (4).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/phenomena.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 4 sealed receipts fold to 7c2c40c6-89f6-8eb8-bc77-10aca5a1c56f. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (7, 5, 2, 8, 4, 2, 0). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: families.lean (5 observed, 1.91 expected, lift 2.61), elementary.lean (3 observed, 1.49 expected, lift 2.01), mechanical.lean (6 observed, 4.77 expected, lift 1.26). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.2 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 49.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.33; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.6. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 83213ac8f1ad (2026-09-15), over 659 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. The SI base quantities and their defining constants are definitions of the Conférence Générale des Poids et Mesures (2019 revision, effective 20 May 2019); the electrochemical results are Michael Faraday's laws of electrolysis, 1834, and the standard enthalpy of combustion of hydrogen. Every physical result named here has an earlier author or a standards body, and none is this deposit's. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. every_phenomenon_is_definitional_or_credited — entries.all (fun e => statusOf e == 0 || statusOf e == 1) record
  2. seven_definitional_and_two_credited — (entries.filter (fun e => statusOf e == 0)).length = 7 ∧ (entries.filter (fun e => statusOf e == 1)).length = 2 ∧ entries.length = 9 record
  3. the_definitional_half_is_the_whole_si — (entries.filter (fun e => statusOf e == 0)).length = 7 record
  4. the_table_is_closed_and_that_is_all_this_file_decides — entries.all (fun e => statusOf e == 0 || statusOf e == 1) ∧ entries.length = 9 ∧ (entries.filter (fun e => statusOf e == 0)).length = 7 record
